title: Start date, End date and term derive; valid through the End date
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as a service advisor with the view customers and create and edit customers permissions.
  2. An asset (e.g. unit 402 · 2019 Freightliner Cascadia of "Aacrest Works") enrolled on a schedule that has a compliance service "CVIP" (Term 12 months), seeded with the standard steps.
  3. Open the asset page; the asset card is on the left and its Compliance section sits below Contact.
  4. Know today's date before you start.
custom_steps:
1. Click + Add record: Term 12 months, Start date 14 Oct 2025; read End date. Cancel.
  2. Click + Add record: Term 12 months, End date 14 Oct 2026; read Start date. Cancel.
  3. Click + Add record: Term 12 months, type Start date 1 Nov 2025, then type End date 30 Sep 2026; read both.
  4. Click + Add record for a certificate issued months ago by another shop: Term 12 months and type Start date 14 Oct 2025 by hand; read End date.
  5. Click + Add record: Term 12 months, leave both dates empty and try to save.
  6. Save a record with Term 12 months and End date = today; read the CVIP row's badge.
  7. Edit that record, set End date = yesterday, save, and read the badge again.
  8. Hover the (i) beside Start date and the (i) beside End date.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • End date fills in as 14 Oct 2026 (same day number, 12 months on).
  • Start date fills in as 14 Oct 2025 (End date less the term).
  • Both typed dates stay as typed (1 Nov 2025 and 30 Sep 2026): a typed date wins over a derived one.
  • The Start date can be typed by hand; End date fills in as 14 Oct 2026.
  • The record cannot be saved with neither date.
  • With End date = today the certificate is still valid: the row reads "Due today", not "Overdue".
  • With End date = yesterday the certificate has lapsed: the row reads "Overdue".
  • On the design the Start date (i) reads "Entered by hand, because it comes from the agency and has nothing to do with when a work order completed." and the End date (i) reads "A certificate is valid through its End date."

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10565 (S8, Compliance inspection records on the asset), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S8 (Term and the two dates; S8-R10, S8-R11, S8-E1, S8-E2); Design board "Chunk 1.dc.html" (MR V2 Claude Design project, version of 6 October 2026), artboard K4; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S8-R10: “End date lands on the same day number: 14 Oct 2025 plus 12 months is 14 Oct 2026”
  • S8-R10: “Start date plus the term fills End date, and End date less the term fills Start date”
  • S8-R10: “A date a person typed always wins over a derived one”
  • S8-E1: “A certificate arrives already months old, issued by another shop. The Start date is entered by hand”
  • S8-R11: “A record needs the term and at least one of the two dates. It cannot be saved with neither”
  • Design board, artboard S1 (Status column hover): “Due today: an exact certificate or calendar date that falls today.”
  • S8-E2: “A certificate is valid through its End date and lapses the day after. A weekend or holiday does not move it”
  • Design board, artboard K4 (Start date (i)): “Entered by hand, because it comes from the agency and has nothing to do with when a work order completed.”
  • Design board, artboard K4 (End date (i)): “A certificate is valid through its End date.”
